title: Identifying essential long non-coding RNAs in cancer using CRISPRi-based dropout screens
author: Bril, Schwarzmueller, et al.
materials: An adequate cell system or cell lines of interest should be initially selected. Any cell line that can be expanded in vitro is in principle suited for this protocol. Our laboratory mainly focuses on colorectal cancer and we, therefore, established this procedure using a panel of CRC cell lines (e.g., Colo320HSR, LS180, HT55 and LS411N). Each cell line is then profiled using GRO-seq. To capture nascent transcripts, millions of cell nuclei are isolated and transcription is reinitiated in presence of an analog of UTP (Br-UTP). Nascent transcripts with incorporated Br-UTP can be captured with an agarose-conjugated anti-BrdU antibody (Santa Cruz, IIB5). This section describes how to isolate cell nuclei, perform and analyze GRO-seq. Steps related to the GRO-Seq protocol are illustrated in Figure 2A.CRITICAL: RNA is sensitive to temperature and enzymatic digestion by RNases, which are normally present on skin, surfaces, etc. Keep all surfaces and equipment clean while performing this protocol. We also recommend to wear gloves and to keep samples on ice whenever indicated in the protocol. Only use RNase-free materials and chemicals.Note: Here we describe the procedure from the day cells are harvested for nuclei isolation. We do not consider seeding density, expansion time and possible treatments. However, if you have different treatments or conditions in your experimental setup, these factors should be carefully considered in the overall planning. For cancer cell lines, we generally harvest 20 × 106 cells per replicate and combine two run-on reactions (each with 5 × 106 nuclei) in order to obtain sufficient material for the preparation of a sequencing library. However, if the transcriptional output of your cells of interest is low, you may have to increase the number of pooled run-on reactions per replicate.Figure 2Global run-on sequencing(A) Scheme highlighting key steps required to perform global run-on sequencing.(B) Example of nuclei obtained from the CRC cell line HCT116, following the procedure illustrated in A1.(C) Analysis of two purified run-on reactions (S1 and S2) using a Bioanalyzer RNA 6000 Pico Chip. The size distribution is indicated by a ladder (L).(D) Electropherograms of samples presented in B. Fragment sizes (nucleotides, nt) are plotted against arbitrary fluorescence units (FU).

steps.title: Prepare RNase‑free workspace
steps.instruction: Clean all surfaces, wear gloves, keep reagents and samples on ice, and use only RNase‑free consumables throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Harvest cells and isolate nuclei
steps.instruction: Grow the chosen cell line (e.g., colorectal cancer lines) and harvest 20 × 10⁶ cells per replicate; isolate nuclei and set up two run‑on reactions each with 5 × 10⁶ nuclei (combined later to obtain sufficient material).

steps.title: Perform GRO‑seq run‑on
steps.instruction: Re‑initiate transcription in the isolated nuclei in the presence of Br‑UTP (a UTP analog) and capture nascent Br‑UTP‑labeled transcripts with agarose‑conjugated anti‑BrdU antibody (Santa Cruz, IIB5).

steps.title: Purify nascent RNA
steps.instruction: Purify the Br‑UTP‑labeled RNA from the antibody‑captured complexes; this step typically takes 7–12 h spread over 3 days.

steps.title: Prepare GRO‑seq library
steps.instruction: Construct sequencing libraries from the purified nascent RNA following standard GRO‑seq protocols (fragmentation, adapter ligation, etc.) and assess library size distribution on a Bioanalyzer RNA 6000 Pico Chip.

steps.title: Set up analysis environment
steps.instruction: On an Ubuntu 20.04 system (WSL 1), create a directory named “CRISPRi”, install Python via Anaconda, and place the supplementary HTML files (Cleanup and guide picking.html, Ordered csv.html, Merge files.html) into that folder.

steps.title: Quality‑control raw reads
steps.instruction: Run FastQC on each raw FASTQ file; green‑flag reads are high quality, yellow‑flag reads may require further attention (e.g., rRNA contamination) and possibly resequencing.

steps.title: Trim low‑quality sequences
steps.instruction: Install Trimmomatic and trim adapters/low‑quality bases according to the FastQC report; command lines will vary depending on the identified issues.

steps.title: Generate STAR reference genome
steps.instruction: Download the GRCh38 primary assembly fasta and the GENCODE long‑noncoding RNA GTF (release XX) with wget; then run STAR with –runThreadN 12, –runMode genomeGenerate, –genomeDir GRCh38_star_index, –genomeFastaFiles GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa, –sjdbGTFfile gencode.vXX.long_noncoding_RNAs.gtf, –sjdbOverhang 149.

steps.title: Align reads with STAR
steps.instruction: Align each high‑quality FASTQ file to the STAR index using 12 threads, output sorted BAM files (e.g., seed_sample.bam) and optional wiggle files as shown in the example command.

steps.title: Run NRSA differential analysis
steps.instruction: Clone the NRSA tool from https://github.com/vermeulenlab/lncRNA/, ensure the genome version matches the STAR index, then execute pause_PROseq.pl and eRNA.pl with the appropriate –in1 and –in2 BAM files (e.g., condition1.bam, condition2.bam) and –m GRCh38; collect the output file gb_change.txt for downstream filtering.

steps.title: Process GRO‑Seq data (2–3 h per sample)
steps.instruction: Execute the FastQC → Trimmomatic → STAR alignment → NRSA pipeline described above; each sample typically requires 2–3 hours of compute time.

steps.title: Clone gRNA library into lentiviral vector
steps.instruction: Insert the pooled gRNA library into the pDECKO‑mCherry backbone (Addgene #78534), which carries mCherry fluorescence and a puromycin resistance cassette; produce lentiviral particles using standard protocols (not detailed here).

steps.title: Transduce CRISPRi cells at low MOI
steps.instruction: Transduce KRAB‑dCas9‑BFP cells with the lentiviral gRNA library at a low multiplicity of infection to favor single integrations; monitor mCherry fluorescence by flow cytometry to adjust virus amount; select transduced cells with puromycin for up to 2 weeks, using both antibiotic selection and fluorescence for confirmation.

steps.title: Collect cell pellets for gDNA
steps.instruction: At the desired time points (day 0, T1, T2), harvest cells, pellet them, and store at –20 °C or proceed directly to genomic DNA extraction.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate genomic DNA from each cell pellet using a Genomic DNA Purification Kit or equivalent product.

steps.title: Amplify gRNA inserts (PCR1)
steps.instruction: Perform PCR1 with primers specific to the vector backbone; ensure library complexity by using at least 200 genome equivalents per gRNA (e.g., for a 10 000‑gRNA library, amplify ≈13 µg gDNA, given 6.5 pg per diploid genome).

steps.title: Add adapters and indices (PCR2)
steps.instruction: Run PCR2 with Illumina adapter‑containing primers (Table S2) to append sequencing adapters and sample indices to the PCR1 amplicons.

steps.title: Purify and quantify libraries
steps.instruction: Gel‑purify PCR2 products using the NucleoSpin Gel & PCR Clean‑up kit; quantify each library with the NEBNext® Library Quant Kit for Illumina®; dilute to a final concentration of 20–50 nM (initially dilute to 40–100 nM, re‑quantify, then dilute to the final range) and pool all libraries for multiplex sequencing.

steps.title: Sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Sequence the pooled libraries on an Illumina platform using single‑end 50 bp reads (SE50), include a 5 % PhiX spike‑in, and aim for at least 200 reads per gRNA.

steps.title: Prepare dropout‑screen analysis environment
steps.instruction: On Ubuntu 20.04 (WSL 1), create a working directory, install R and RStudio, and install Java (default‑jre) required for Trimmomatic.

steps.title: Trim gRNA reads
steps.instruction: Download Trimmomatic‑0.39 via wget, unzip, and run: java -jar ./Trimmomatic-0.39.jar SE -threads 16 $FILE.fastq ./Trimmed/$FILE_Trim.fastq HEADCROP:22 CROP:19 (example); a bash loop can process all *.fastq files; verify cropping with head; note that an alternative command shown in the protocol uses CROP:19144.

steps.title: Count guides with MAGeCK
steps.instruction: Download MAGeCK 0.5.9.4, extract and install with python setup.py install; prepare a CSV library file with columns seqID, gRNAs, targetgene (as in Table 5); run mageck count –l library.csv --fastq *.fastq in the Trimmed folder; this generates .count.txt and .count_summary.txt files.

steps.title: Visualize dropout results
steps.instruction: Use the R package EnhancedVolcano (or similar) to generate volcano plots of log₂ fold‑change versus –log₁₀ p‑value, confirming that negative controls do not drop out while positive controls do.

description: This protocol describes the nascent RNA profiling of in vitro-cultured cell lines with subsequent functional assessment of selected transcripts using a CRISPRi-based screening approach. While we established this procedure using a panel of colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines (e.g., Colo320HSR, LS180, HT55, LS411N), most in vitro-cultured cellular models can be used. A schematic overview of the workflow is shown in Figure 1.Figure 1Workflow to assess the function of expressed/selected lncRNAs with CRISPRi dropout screensThe schematic illustrates essential steps for each section of the protocol, including 1-Target identification, 2-CRISPRi screen and 3-Screen analysis.
